question: What is the IUPAC name of the compound CH₃NH₂?
solution: The correct answer is __**Methanamine**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • Methylamine (CH₃NH₂) is a **simple amine**, which is a derivative of ammonia (NH₃) where one hydrogen atom is replaced by a methyl group (CH₃). • Methylamine is a colorless gas at room temperature with a strong, fishy odor. • It is **highly soluble in water** due to its ability to form hydrogen bonds. • Methylamine is used in the production of various chemicals, including pharmaceuticals, pesticides, and surfactants. It is also involved in the synthesis of other amines and is used in organic chemistry as a reagent. • As an amine, methylamine **can act as a base **and can participate in nucleophilic substitution reactions, making it an important building block in organic synthesis. • Methylamine is flammable and can be **toxic **if inhaled or ingested.
